doc.title: Houston Person Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Early listening and tenor influences
summary: Person recalls buying 78s in the South and lists tenor influences led by Illinois Jacquet, plus Archia, Griffin, Mobley, Ammons, Getz, Marsh, Holiday and Percy France; he likes organ and piano groups alike.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Who did you buy when you were young, that you were listening to, and were they on 78’s at that time?
Oh yeah, yeah. Dinah Washington, Buddy Johnson, Stan Kenton. I was in the south. Yeah, Stan Kenton, Dizzy Gillespie. Just about everybody — Lester Young — they were all on 78’s. And then the LP came.
Who in particular on tenor did you feel that you might have been influenced by?
Well I liked everybody really, starting with Illinois Jacquet. And it’s funny, when you’re out of New York you get a better feel of what really — see being in the south I got all

those different influences, Gospel, blues — so I liked Tom Archia, you know, the guy who worked with Wynonie Harris, and then there was Johnny Griffin with Hot Lips, and other guys played in R&B things. Willis Jackson. And then I liked Hank Mobley, just everybody, I liked everybody. But now my initial influence I would say would have to be probably Illinois Jacquet. But I liked Lester Young, Gene Ammons, and I liked Stan Getz and I like Warne Marsh a lot, and I liked another saxophone player that used to be from Newark, I never knew what happened to him, Joe Holiday. And another one of my big influences was Percy France, he used to play with Bill Doggett in the organ groups. So there was all kinds of influences out there.
People seem to associate you a lot with organ groups, but that’s only part of what you did.
Yeah. I like organ groups, I like piano groups. I like anything that’s swinging and is bluesy.
